book_title: Founding Sales (Chapters 7-13 and Conclusion; Part B of a two-agent split)

frameworks.name: Sales call structure: plan, discover, qualify, demonstrate, prove, price, ask
frameworks.decision: How to run a first sales conversation (call or meeting) so it either advances with an agreed next step or ends early and politely.
evidence_required: what the lead asked for and how they arrived
public facts about the account (site, listings, job posts)
offer facts: price ranges, proof items, case results
prerequisites: A deal size that pays for a live conversation (BRP-19 motion fit)
Confirmed facts for price and proof; otherwise [NEEDS FACT]

branches.if: Demo or walkthrough under ~15 minutes, or qualification is visible from public facts
branches.then: One combined meeting: discovery, short demo, proof, price, ask.

branches.if: Demo is long (30-60 min) and qualification needs questions
branches.then: Separate short discovery call; book the demo only if qualified.

branches.if: Discovery shows no pain or no ability to pay
branches.then: End politely, give time back, offer one useful resource; log as unqualified with reason.

branches.if: Contact likes it but cannot decide
branches.then: Agree on a joint follow-up that includes the decision-maker; send a forwardable summary.

branches.if: Buyer asks price early in an enquiry
branches.then: Give the confirmed range plainly (small-business norm), then frame it against their stated problem.

steps: Pre-call note (10-15 min): pain signals, size of the job, current solution, who decides, known unknowns, call goal.
Open: agree the agenda and that the call may end early if it is not a fit (micro-contract).
Discovery: problem, size, current workaround and its cost, consequence of doing nothing, who uses it, who decides, how they buy, timing.
Qualify or offramp.
Show only what maps to their stated problem, using their data or realistic sample data.
Proof: one or two results from confirmed facts.
Price framed against their current cost or alternative; then stop talking.
Direct ask, or a trial close if signals are unclear.
Agree and calendar the next step; same-day summary email.
exceptions_failure_modes: Feature tour without discovery ('show up and throw up')
Skipping the price and the ask out of fear of rejection
Re-asking questions already answered in research
Persona mismatch (pitching ROI to a user, features to an executive)
Over-preparing for low-value calls where a self-serve path fits better

requirements.labor: owner time: ~15 min prep + call + ~15 min follow-up per meeting
requirements.capability: a short pitch narrative and 1-2 proof items
requirements.measurement: meetings held, qualified share, next-step agreed share, proposals requested

metrics: share ending with a calendared next step
guardrails: No invented prices, results or customers
No pressure or false urgency
Recording or transcription only with consent where law requires
Use only business-relevant public facts in research (no personal social-media profiling)
stop_review: Review the script after every ~10 held meetings: which questions predicted wins, which slides confused
alternatives: Low price or no time for calls: recorded demo video, published FAQ/objections page, self-serve trial (BRP-19)
No proof yet: offer a small paid first project instead of claiming results
frameworks.interpretation: Interpretation: Kazanjy's sequence is a practical script skeleton that ClimbOS currently lacks; sales-follow-up covers enquiry replies and quote follow-up, and Book 11 covers discovery and demo principles but not the order of a live call or the split rule.

proposed_rules.rule: proposed: A sales-call plan must end with one agreed, dated next step or an explicit disqualification; 'I'll send info, let me know' is not a next step.
proposed: Recommend a separate discovery call only when the demo needs more than ~15 minutes; otherwise one meeting (each extra meeting adds no-show risk).
proposed: Call plans never include recording or transcription unless the owner confirms consent handling for the jurisdiction.
proposed: Do not draft live-call scripts when the price per customer cannot pay for a human sale; route to BRP-19 alternatives.

frameworks.climbos_location: skills/sales-follow-up/SKILL.md (candidate v2: new 'Live sales call' section); Book 11 §3, §5

relation_to_existing.note: Book 11 states discovery/demo principles (SPIN, demo vs pilot); sales-follow-up step 4 has a 2-minute phone script only. This adds the full call order, the split rule and the offramp.

frameworks.disagreements: Kazanjy advises holding price until value is framed; sales-follow-up step 3 answers price directly in first replies. Decide by context: an inbound small-business enquiry asking price gets the confirmed range; a complex B2B evaluation may frame price after discovery but never dodges a direct question. Kazanjy's 'credible threat' of going over the contact's head and personal-interest icebreakers are not adopted.

frameworks.name: Qualification for small-business and new-category deals
frameworks.decision: Whether to keep investing time in an opportunity, and which missing fact to get next.
evidence_required: stated problem in the buyer's words
evidence the problem is material (volume, cost, deadline)
whether the buyer pays for any solution to this or similar problems
who decides and how purchases happen
timing or trigger
prerequisites: A written ideal-customer description with disqualifiers (Book 11 §2)

branches.if: No real problem, or problem is trivial for them
branches.then: Disqualify with reason; log as unqualified (feedback to targeting).

branches.if: Problem real, but the organisation never pays for tools/services to fix problems
branches.then: Disqualify or park; this is not a 'budget objection'.

branches.if: Problem real and they pay for alternatives, but no budget line for this offer
branches.then: Keep: new-category offers rarely have a budget line; look for existing spend on the problem.

branches.if: Problem real, contact lacks authority
branches.then: Keep; agree a joint meeting with the decision-maker.

branches.if: Problem real, no urgency or trigger
branches.then: Agreed deferral with a date the buyer chooses, not active pipeline.

steps: Record each qualification field as unknown / reported / verified / contradicted (Book 11 §4 states).
Ask the cheapest missing question next.
Disqualify early and politely.
Review 'unqualified after meeting' cases monthly to fix targeting or booking questions.
exceptions_failure_modes: Strict BANT applied to a category buyers did not know existed
Treating a friendly contact as the decision-maker
Selling to buyers who will get little value because they agreed to a low price (churn later)
metrics: share of held meetings later marked unqualified
guardrails: Job title does not prove authority; stage label does not prove probability (Book 11 prohibited inferences)
Never mark a field verified from a similar customer
stop_review: If unqualified-after-meeting share is high for two review periods, fix targeting or booking questions before adding more outreach
alternatives: Too few deals to compute shares: review each lost/unqualified deal by hand
frameworks.interpretation: Interpretation: Kazanjy's relaxation of BANT for new categories, plus the 'do they buy any tools at all' test and the Closed-Unqualified stage, are the useful additions. Book 11's evidence-state model is better for recording; Kazanjy supplies the small-deal branching.

proposed_rules.rule: proposed: 'No budget line' alone never disqualifies; 'never pays for solutions to problems like this' does, unless the owner overrides.
proposed: Track 'unqualified after a meeting' separately from 'lost'; a rising share points to targeting or booking questions (diagnostic hypothesis, not proven cause).
proposed: Do not recommend discounting to win a buyer whose expected value from the offer is low; recommend disqualifying.

frameworks.climbos_location: Book 11 §4 (candidate v2 small-deal branch); skills/sales-follow-up/SKILL.md; convex/crm.ts stages

relation_to_existing.note: Book 11 uses MEDDPICC for complex deals and says simple deals need a lighter path but does not define it; this supplies that lighter path.

frameworks.disagreements: None material with Book 11; Kazanjy is less cautious about inferring 'they're hiding the real objection'. Book 11 §6 warns not to assume concealment; ClimbOS keeps Book 11's stance and asks once.

frameworks.name: Objection and trial-request handling (live loop vs written follow-up)
frameworks.decision: How to respond to a specific hesitation, and when to stop.
evidence_required: the objection in the buyer's words
discovery facts
proof items and pricing rules in confirmed facts
prerequisites: A living objection list with approved answers and proof (owner-maintained)

branches.if: Vague no ('not a fit')
branches.then: Ask once what specifically blocks progress.

branches.if: Price: gap small (around 10% in the author's example)
branches.then: Treat as negotiation; use K6 levers within owner-approved limits.

branches.if: Price: gap large (around 50%)
branches.then: Walk the value math with the buyer's own numbers; if their numbers show low value, offer a smaller scope or disqualify.

branches.if: 'No need' despite earlier evidence of need
branches.then: Restate the evidence they gave and ask which part is wrong; accept a specific contradiction.

branches.if: Status quo / fear of change
branches.then: Show the cost of no change using the buyer's own numbers; describe how onboarding will be handled.

branches.if: Timing / other priorities
branches.then: Reduce perceived effort; offer a later start date if real; or agree a deferral date.

branches.if: 'Need a trial'
branches.then: Ask what proof would settle it; offer case evidence, a guided hands-on session, or (large deals only) a structured pilot with success criteria and owner time limits.

branches.if: Written (async) channel and the buyer repeats the no
branches.then: Stop; gracious close (sales-follow-up and reply-handling rule).

steps: Catch the objection and restate it.
Find the question under the question.
Answer with one concrete proof or the buyer's own numbers.
Check the answer landed.
Return to the next step; in a live conversation, check for other blockers.
exceptions_failure_modes: Arguing or repeating the pitch
Unstructured free trials for products that need setup (low use, blamed on product)
Unrequested discounts
Treating every objection as a hidden different objection

requirements.cash: none; structured pilot costs owner time
requirements.capability: proof library, ROI inputs from buyer
requirements.measurement: objection frequency by type; pilot conversion

metrics: share of trial requests resolved by proof without a pilot
guardrails: One attempt per objection in written follow-ups
No invented discounts, deadlines or results
Pilot success criteria agreed in writing before start
stop_review: Any objection heard 2+ times: add an approved answer and proof item to the living list
Very frequent objection: address it up front in the pitch or landing page
alternatives: No proof items yet: offer a small paid first step or money-back terms if the owner approves
Self-serve product: a time-boxed trial with onboarding emails instead of a guided session
frameworks.interpretation: Interpretation: Kazanjy's loop assumes a live, engaged buyer. ClimbOS's 'one attempt' rule governs asynchronous drafts. Both hold if scoped by channel.

proposed_rules.rule: proposed: For price objections, ask the size of the gap before answering; route small gaps to negotiation levers and large gaps to value math or scope change.
proposed: Never recommend an unstructured free trial for an offer that needs setup or training; recommend a guided session or a structured pilot with written success criteria.
proposed: Structured pilots only when expected deal value covers the owner hours of the pilot (computed by code from owner inputs).
proposed: In written follow-ups, one evidenced answer per objection; a repeated no ends the sequence.

relation_to_existing.note: Adds the price-gap diagnostic, the 'no budget' disqualifier test, trial-request handling and the live loop; keeps the one-attempt rule for async.

frameworks.disagreements: Kazanjy: loop until no objections remain, and treat vague 'no need' as cover for a hidden objection. sales-follow-up/reply-handling: one attempt, never argue. Book 11 §6: don't assume concealment. Resolution: channel decides (live vs written) and the buyer's explicit repeat no is final in both. Kazanjy's 'fear of missing out / competitors already use it' framing is allowed only with true, sourced facts.

frameworks.name: Next-step contracts, stalled deals and close-lost discipline
frameworks.decision: When a deal is still alive, when to close it as lost, and whether and when to re-engage.
evidence_required: agreed next steps and dates
kept vs broken commitments (missed meetings, unanswered agreed deliverables)
explicit buyer statements about timing or permission to re-contact
prerequisites: Deals carry next step + date (convex/crm.ts nextStep/nextStepAt exist)

branches.if: Next step agreed and dated
branches.then: Keep active; deliver your part within a day.

branches.if: One missed meeting
branches.then: Reschedule once with a specific time.

branches.if: Two or more broken commitments or no reply after an agreed step
branches.then: Send one respectful clarity email (still a priority? bad time? not a fit?), then close as lost with reason if no answer.

branches.if: Buyer says 'not now' with a date
branches.then: Close as deferred; one check-in on that date (permission given).

branches.if: Buyer says 'not now' without a date
branches.then: Ask permission for a later check-in; no re-contact without it.

branches.if: Buyer opts out or says stop
branches.then: Suppress; no re-engagement ever from automation.

steps: State the next step, owner and date at the end of every interaction and confirm it in writing.
Deliver your part fast.
Detect broken commitments from the calendar and CRM.
Clarity email draft for owner approval.
Close lost with reason(s) (multi-select, unknown allowed) and notes.
Schedule permitted re-engagement as a new opportunity.
exceptions_failure_modes: Leaving dead deals open (inflates pipeline, wastes owner time)
Guilt-tripping breakup emails
Re-contacting without permission
Single forced loss reason

requirements.capability: CRM with next step/date and lost reason
requirements.measurement: deals without next step; broken-commitment count

metrics: share of open deals with a dated next step
deals closed lost per month by reason
guardrails: Re-contact only with permission or a lawful basis (consent rules vary by country)
Breakup email: no guilt, no false deadline (sales-follow-up Never do)
Owner approves every send
stop_review: Monthly: read lost reasons; recurring reason becomes a positioning, offer or targeting question
alternatives: No CRM use: a weekly 10-minute list review of open quotes with next-step dates
frameworks.interpretation: Interpretation: 'broken micro-contracts' is a cheap, observable leading signal of a dying deal that ClimbOS can compute (missed booking, past-due nextStepAt).

proposed_rules.rule: proposed: An open deal with no future dated next step is flagged 'uncovered' in the pipeline view and daily brief.
proposed: Two broken commitments trigger a suggested clarity email, owner-approved, then close-lost with reason if unanswered.
proposed: Re-engagement of a lost or deferred deal requires buyer permission or a lawful basis recorded on the deal; no default 60-day re-contact.

frameworks.climbos_location: convex/crm.ts (deal flags); skills/sales-follow-up/SKILL.md step 8; skills/reply-handling/SKILL.md 'Not now'

relation_to_existing.note: Book 11 already requires next action/owner/date and separates deferred from lost. Adds the broken-commitment trigger and the clarity-email step.

frameworks.disagreements: Kazanjy: if no date was given, re-engage after ~60 days regardless. ClimbOS reply-handling ('without permission, no further contact') and Book 11 §13 ('avoid indefinite automated reminders') win; for cold contacts this is also a legal matter (e.g. UK/EU direct-marketing rules).

frameworks.name: Pipeline stages, hygiene and conversion metrics; is the pipeline the binding constraint?
frameworks.decision: For a business that sells through calls, quotes or proposals: which pipeline step limits revenue, and therefore whether to add more meetings (demand) or fix conversion, offer, targeting or selling capacity.
evidence_required: per period: meetings booked, meetings held, proposals/quotes sent, won, lost, unqualified, average won value
owner selling hours per week and maximum meetings the owner can hold
deal dates (created, stage changes, won/lost)
prerequisites: Stage definitions with entry criteria the owner agrees to
At least a few closed decisions; otherwise use per-deal review, not rates

branches.if: Held/booked is low (owner's own history or target)
branches.then: Meeting quality or reminders problem: confirmations, reminders, booking-page qualification (constraint: conversion of booked meetings).

branches.if: Unqualified-after-meeting share is high
branches.then: Targeting/positioning: tighten who gets a meeting before adding volume (competing explanation: booking form too loose).

branches.if: Held -> proposal low, qualified
branches.then: Discovery/pitch problem or offer unclear (conversion/offer).

branches.if: Proposal -> won low
branches.then: Price, packaging, proof or follow-up gap (conversion/offer); check lost reasons.

branches.if: Win rate per held meeting is at or above the owner's own target and the owner's calendar has room
branches.then: Pipeline volume (demand) is the binding constraint: add qualified meetings.

branches.if: Owner's calendar is full and win rate is falling
branches.then: Selling capacity binds (delivery): cap new meetings, delegate appointment setting or raise price; do not add demand.

branches.if: Fewer than ~5 closed decisions in the window
branches.then: Rates are unknown; review deals individually and keep collecting.

steps: Count stages over a fixed window (code).
Compute hold rate, held->proposal, proposal->won, win per held meeting, unqualified share, median days to close (code).
Compare to the owner's own prior period or stated target; external benchmarks only as grade-D context, never as a verdict.
Name the weakest link and its competing explanation.
Daily hygiene: uncovered deals, late-stage deals untouched 7+ days, deals stuck past the owner's typical stage time, past-due next steps.
Prioritise follow-up from closest-to-money down, by value.
exceptions_failure_modes: Stage labels that describe seller activity instead of buyer progress
Using CRM default stage probabilities as forecasts
Small samples read as rates
Comparing immature and mature cohorts (recent deals have not had time to close)
Adding outreach when conversion or capacity is the limit

requirements.labor: minutes per week to keep stages true
requirements.capability: CRM stages with dates; deterministic aggregation

metrics: win rate per held first meeting
pipeline value (open, unweighted) and won value
guardrails: All arithmetic in code
No stage-default probabilities (Book 11 prohibited inference)
Benchmarks from this book are grade D and dated
Diagnosis hypothesis, not proven cause
stop_review: Re-diagnose each month or after 10 new closed decisions
If the named constraint does not move after one cycle of fixes, test the competing explanation
alternatives: No CRM data: ask the owner for the six counts for the last 60-90 days
Very low volume: qualitative review of the last 5 won and 5 lost deals
frameworks.interpretation: Interpretation: Kazanjy's revenue identity (opportunities x win rate x deal size), his carrying-load signal (falling close rate when overloaded) and his readiness rule (fix win rate before adding volume) combine into a sales-pipeline branch of ClimbOS's diagnosis, which today only reads visitors -> leads -> activated -> customers.

proposed_rules.rule: proposed: For sales-led businesses, diagnosis reads a sales block (booked, held, proposals, won, lost, unqualified, value, owner meeting capacity) and names the weakest link in code.

proposed: Do not recommend more top-of-funnel outreach when win rate per held meeting is below the owner's own target or prior period, unless the owner's calendar is empty and sample size is adequate.
proposed: When the owner's meeting capacity is >=80% used and win rate is falling, name selling capacity (delivery) as the constraint.
proposed: Kazanjy's 15-30% win-rate band may be shown only as 'author view, 2020, venture SaaS, grade D'; it never sets a weak/ok verdict.
proposed: Fewer than 5 closed decisions in the window => rates reported as counts with 'too few to judge'.

frameworks.climbos_location: shared/agents/diagnosis.ts (new sales stage); convex/crm.ts (hygiene flags); convex/jobs.ts:971 (feed CRM data); Book 11 §7

relation_to_existing.note: Book 11 §7 already lists the metrics and warns about weighted pipeline; nothing in code computes them or feeds diagnosis.

frameworks.disagreements: Kazanjy treats 15-30% as a good win rate and uses it to decide readiness to scale; ClimbOS base-rates.md has no sales-led benchmark and diagnosis.ts only uses base-rates references. Owner's own history decides; the book band is context only. Book 11 favours buyer-progress stage names; Kazanjy's TalentBin stages mix seller activity ('Demo Scheduled') and buyer progress. Use Book 11's naming with Kazanjy's 'unqualified' and 'contract sent' states.

frameworks.name: Negotiation levers, payment terms and proposal options
frameworks.decision: What to trade when a ready-to-buy client wants a better deal, and how to structure options and payment terms.
evidence_required: owner's list price, floor price and margin (shared/analysis/decisions.ts margin/priceFloor)
which terms the owner is willing to vary
competitor quote if claimed (seen, not assumed)
prerequisites: Owner-approved price rules; the AI never invents a discount

branches.if: Buyer wants a lower unit price
branches.then: Offer it only in exchange for more units, longer term or upfront payment, within owner limits.

branches.if: Buyer wants a lower total
branches.then: Reduce scope or term rather than discounting the same scope.

branches.if: Buyer wants monthly or split payments
branches.then: Price split payments above upfront (owner sets the premium).

branches.if: Buyer cites a cheaper competitor
branches.then: Compare like for like; adjust only if the quote is shown and the owner approves; tie any match to signing now.

branches.if: Buyer just wants to feel they won
branches.then: A small, owner-pre-approved concession with no change to cash terms can close it.

steps: List levers and owner priorities (cash up front, then term, then price).
Concede one step at a time; always trade.
Compute effective price and premium in code.
Document any non-standard concession and its reason in the agreement.
Proposal options: only offers the owner would deliver; each option viable.
exceptions_failure_modes: Negotiating against yourself before the buyer asks
Reverse auction with a competitor
Concessions that break delivery capacity or margin floor
Decoy options that are deliberately unusable

requirements.measurement: average discount, payment-term mix, days to cash

guardrails: No false urgency: 'price goes up' or 'limited start slots' only if true and in facts
Discounts only from owner rules
Never below price floor
Consumer contracts: check local cancellation and payment-term law
stop_review: If average realised discount keeps rising, review list price and proof rather than conceding more
alternatives: No price rules from owner: present list price and ask the owner before any concession
frameworks.interpretation: Interpretation: the trade-don't-give principle and the cash-first lever order are sound for cash-constrained small businesses; the anchoring and urgency tactics need ClimbOS's honesty filters.

proposed_rules.rule: proposed: Every concession in a drafted negotiation reply is paired with something the client gives (volume, term, upfront payment, reduced scope).
proposed: Effective price, payment-term premium and margin after concession are computed in code and checked against the owner's price floor.
proposed: Urgency statements (price rise, limited slots, offer end date) require a matching fact; otherwise the lint blocks them.
proposed: Proposal options must each be a deliverable offer; no decoy options.

relation_to_existing.note: Book 11 says trade value and obligations explicitly; this adds lever priority and payment-term math.

frameworks.disagreements: Kazanjy: start with inflated pricing to leave room, and design three options so the middle is the target and the top looks like a deal. Book 11 §6: no intentionally unusable option to steer. Kazanjy also suggests 'pricing may go up' and 'CS slots are limited' as urgency; sales-follow-up forbids these without a fact. ClimbOS keeps its rules: anchoring is a strategic preference the owner may choose with real prices; fabricated urgency is never drafted. Author's own short-term pricing example (1.43x per month) does not meet his stated 2-3x rule; treat the multiple as owner choice.

frameworks.name: High-touch onboarding, success reviews and renewals (B2B and agencies)
frameworks.decision: How a small B2B business or agency gets new clients to the promised result and protects renewal, and whether its price can carry that work.
evidence_required: what was promised in the sale (goals, KPIs)
onboarding steps and owner/staff hours per client
usage or delivery signals per client
contract term and renewal date
prerequisites: Sale notes captured at close: decision-maker, users, goals

branches.if: Onboarding labour cost per client is a large share of first-period revenue
branches.then: Charge a setup fee, simplify onboarding, or move to self-serve materials (code computes the share).

branches.if: Setup blockers exist (access, integrations, data)
branches.then: Separate setup call first, then the working session.

branches.if: Client misses onboarding sessions
branches.then: Reschedule immediately; track who has not onboarded.

branches.if: Value signals low for a client
branches.then: Helpful check-in; most effort on middling clients; involve the sponsor if one user blocks.

branches.if: Price per client is low
branches.then: Automated success summary (e.g. a client report link) instead of a meeting.

branches.if: Renewal near and issues open
branches.then: Renewal conversation ~6 weeks before term end; fix plan or short extension (owner choice).

steps: Kickoff: restate goals ('rediscovery') and confirm in writing.
Setup items first.
Client does real work in the session.
Measurable homework; back-check booked ~2 weeks out before ending.
Monitor value signals; record outcomes with dates.
Quarterly (or automated) success review: goals, before/after KPIs, issues, next steps.
Renewal conversation and ask; expansion only if delivering.
exceptions_failure_modes: Group onboarding that leaves half-trained users
Upselling while delivery is failing
Losing the sponsor contact; not noticing a champion left
Auto-renew without notice where law requires it

requirements.labor: owner/staff hours per client; must be priced in
requirements.measurement: onboarded on time, first-result date, review held, renewal outcome

metrics: share of new clients onboarded within N days
share with a success review in the last quarter
guardrails: Auto-renewal terms and notices follow local consumer/contract law (external)
Success reports show measured outcomes only, no invented results
Customer stories/testimonials only with client permission
stop_review: If renewal rate falls, review onboarding completion and first-result timing first
alternatives: One-off local consumer jobs: use retention-lifecycle rebooking/review flows instead of QBRs
No usage data: monthly 2-question check-in email
frameworks.interpretation: Interpretation: retention-lifecycle covers automated flows by business type but not the high-touch B2B onboarding and review cadence an agency or consultancy runs; convex/clientReports.ts already provides the 'automated success review' artifact Kazanjy recommends for lower-priced accounts.

proposed_rules.rule: proposed: Before recommending a high-touch onboarding, code computes onboarding labour cost per client and its share of first-period revenue; flag when it exceeds the owner's margin room.
proposed: Every onboarding plan ends with a booked back-check and a measurable first task.
proposed: Expansion or upsell suggestions are suppressed for clients with open delivery issues.
proposed: Auto-renewal clauses and reminder timing are flagged for the owner to check against local law; ClimbOS does not draft them as compliant.

frameworks.climbos_location: skills/retention-lifecycle/SKILL.md (candidate v2: 'High-touch B2B/agency onboarding and renewals'); convex/clientReports.ts

relation_to_existing.note: Activation as value received (BRP-07) matches Kazanjy's 'success = delivering the promise'; adds sessions, homework, reviews and renewal timing.

frameworks.disagreements: Kazanjy recommends auto-renew clauses by default; ClimbOS treats them as owner/legal decisions. His churn chart is hypothetical and not reproducible; do not cite its figures as evidence.

frameworks.name: When to add sellers: founder-led proof, specialisation order and the metric tree
frameworks.decision: Whether a small B2B business or agency should hire sales help now, which role first, and how to diagnose a selling shortfall.
evidence_required: founder win rate per held meeting over enough decisions
average deal value and cycle length
owner time split (prospecting vs selling vs delivery)
cost of the hire
prerequisites: Retention evidence that won clients get value (K7)

branches.if: Too few closed decisions or win rate unstable
branches.then: Keep founder-led selling; do not hire.

branches.if: Win rate stable and owner calendar under-filled because prospecting eats time
branches.then: Appointment setting help first (internal or assistant).

branches.if: Owner calendar full of selling meetings
branches.then: Second closer, or raise price.

branches.if: Onboarding/delivery eats selling time
branches.then: Customer success or delivery help first.

branches.if: Revenue shortfall
branches.then: Trace the metric tree: deals x value; deals = opportunities x win rate; opportunities = activity x conversion.

steps: Compute expected bookings per seller = meetings per month x win rate x deal value (code).
Compute cost of sales = seller cost / bookings (code).
Compare against owner's margin room, not a generic band.
Hire one role, document the motion, review ramp metrics.
exceptions_failure_modes: Premature scaling: hiring sales to 'figure it out'
Lagged scaling: founder keeps closing when the motion is proven
Hiring for a different sales-cycle tempo

requirements.capability: documented pitch, objection list, qualification rules
requirements.measurement: per-seller hold rate, win rate, deal size, activity

metrics: ramp time to founder-level win rate
guardrails: Arithmetic in code
Book salary and cost-of-sales bands are dated US venture-SaaS context, grade D
Employment law and contractor rules vary (external)
stop_review: If a new seller's win rate stays well below founder level after a set ramp, review onboarding before hiring more
alternatives: Can't afford a hire: freelance appointment setter on a trial, partners/referrals, or raise price to free founder time (PB-capacity, PB-price-increase)
frameworks.interpretation: Interpretation: most ClimbOS owners are solo; the useful part is the decision not to hire before the motion is proven, the role-order logic, and the metric tree for diagnosis. Management cadence and comp detail are out of scope.

proposed_rules.rule: proposed: Do not recommend hiring a salesperson until the owner has a stable win rate over enough closed decisions and evidence won clients succeed.
proposed: The first sales hire targets the step that limits the owner's selling time (prospecting, selling or delivery), computed from the owner's time split.
proposed: Hiring recommendations show expected bookings and cost of sales computed from the owner's own rates, with ramp time stated as an assumption.

relation_to_existing.note: PB-capacity addresses delivery capacity; nothing addresses selling capacity or sales hiring readiness.

frameworks.disagreements: Kazanjy's 20-30% cost-of-sales target is venture-SaaS; an agency's gross margin and a consultancy's utilisation differ, so ClimbOS uses the owner's margin, not the band.

skill_proposals.change: Candidate v2: add a 'Live sales call' section (pre-call note, agenda micro-contract, discovery list, offramp, tailored demo, one proof item, price framed against their cost, direct ask, dated next step, same-day summary). Scope step 6: one attempt per objection applies to written follow-ups; a live engaged conversation may address distinct objections in turn. Add price-gap question, 'no budget' disqualifier test and trial-request handling. Add 'send a proposal only when the buyer says they want to buy' and 'every option must be deliverable'.
skill_proposals.why: No skill covers the live call; Kazanjy supplies the order and the split rule.

skill_proposals.change: Add reply types 'asks for a trial' (ask what proof they need; guided session or structured pilot) and 'asks for a proposal' (confirm intent and options). Add a clarity-email draft when two agreed meetings were missed.
skill_proposals.why: Common positive-but-risky replies are not classified today.

skill_proposals.change: Add a 'High-touch B2B and agency clients' branch: kickoff rediscovery, setup-first, measurable first task, booked back-check, monitored value signals, quarterly or automated success review (link to client reports), renewal conversation ~6 weeks before term end, onboarding cost check.
skill_proposals.why: Current skill is automated-flow centred; agencies and consultancies retain clients through sessions and reviews.

skill_proposals.change: Optional: add a 'Sales-led (author views, grade D)' block: demo hold expectation >=80%, per-meeting miss 10-20%, win 10-30% for new B2B solutions, cost of sales 20-30% (Kazanjy 2020, venture SaaS). Mark 'context only; never a verdict'.
skill_proposals.why: Diagnosis needs to state that no reliable sales-led benchmark exists; listing the dated author view with its grade prevents silent reuse.

skill_proposals.change: Add a sales-hiring readiness check: no sales hire before a stable founder win rate and evidence won clients succeed; first hire targets the step limiting the owner's selling time.
skill_proposals.why: Prevents premature-scaling advice for solo owners.

code_gaps.gap: OwnerFunnel only has visitors, leads, activated, newCustomers; sales-led businesses (agencies, consultancies, quote-based services) have no fields for meetings booked/held, proposals, lost, unqualified, deal value or owner meeting capacity.
code_gaps.proposed_change: Add an optional `sales` block {meetingsBooked, meetingsHeld, proposals, won, lost, unqualified, avgWonValue, ownerMaxMeetings, prior?: {...}}.

code_gaps.gap: StageReading.stage has no sales stage and diagnose() cannot name a sales-pipeline constraint; with only leads and newCustomers for a non-SaaS business the verdict is 'unknown' or falls through to demand.
code_gaps.proposed_change: Add readings for hold rate, held->proposal, proposal->won, unqualified share and selling capacity; map to existing constraints (conversion, positioning, delivery, demand) per K5 branches; verdict 'unknown' unless compared to the owner's prior period or target; 'too few' below 5 closed decisions.

code_gaps.gap: diagnose() receives only owner-typed job.business.funnel; CRM deal data in convex/crm.ts is never aggregated into the diagnosis.
code_gaps.proposed_change: Deterministic aggregation of deals by stage and dates over the period into the sales block, owner-confirmable before use.

code_gaps.gap: No lost reason, no stage history or stage-entered timestamps, no 'unqualified' outcome, no proposal/quote stage, no re-contact permission field.
code_gaps.proposed_change: Add lostReasons (multi, incl. unknown), stageHistory [{stage, at}], outcome 'unqualified', optional 'proposal' stage, recontactPermission {allowed, at, untilDate}.

code_gaps.gap: Stages lead/talking/booked/won/lost: 'booked' does not distinguish booked from held; list totals give open count and unweighted value only; no hygiene flags (uncovered, untouched N days, stuck in stage, past-due next step).
code_gaps.proposed_change: Compute flags in the list query from nextStepAt, updatedAt and stage timestamps; surface in pipeline view and get_pipeline tool (convex/lib/climbTools.ts:233-243).

code_gaps.gap: No calculator for payment-term premium/effective price after concessions, or onboarding labour cost per client vs price.
code_gaps.proposed_change: Add `paymentTerms` (upfront vs instalments premium) and `serviceCostShare` (hours x rate / price per period) kinds to CalcInput.

code_gaps.gap: playStage maps 'sales call|proposal|close rate' to conversion but not 'discovery call', 'demo', 'follow-up', 'objection', 'pipeline', so such plays default to demand and can fail the diagnosis-fit lint wrongly.
code_gaps.proposed_change: Extend the conversion regex with discovery call, demo, objection, follow-up cadence, pipeline review.
